definition: Hypnotic susceptibility is a person’s tendency to show hypnotic responses during a standardized hypnosis procedure. In this source, it is assessed with the Harvard Group Scale of Hypnotic Susceptibility, which uses a set trance induction followed by 12 hypnotic phenomena.

reasons: The packet supports the Harvard Group Scale of Hypnotic Susceptibility as a standardized hypnosis test with a trance induction followed by 12 hypnotic phenomena, but it does not explicitly define hypnotic susceptibility as a person’s general tendency to show hypnotic responses.
The definition adds a broader clinical/general characterization that is not stated in the source packet; the source only describes how the test is administered and used for measurement.
